subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single, efficient TypeScript module for an armoured convoy hauler—a heavy six-wheel truck with an armoured cab, sealed glowing cargo pod, roof turret, neon accents and skirts, all in a low-poly cyberpunk style, built with basic box geometry parts to keep the code compact.

I'm sketching the dimensions and joint layout: a ~9m long, 2.6m wide, 3.2m tall chassis, three wheel axles with hinge joints, turret yaw/pitch joints, and simplified helper functions for boxes and cylinders with bone attachment and rotation. For materials, I'm planning a custom gunmetal paint with panel seams using noise and mottling helpers from the paint toolkit.

I'll bump paint size to 2048 for texture clarity, then plan decals: hazard stripes, a hexagon-eye emblem, cargo warning text, a neon sign, and a visor texture for the cab, each applied as textured planes with glow where needed. Now laying out the chassis frame along the z-axis starting from the root joint.

Positioning the six wheels symmetrically at x ±1.15 with dark tyres, steel rims, and a glowing cyan hub ring, plus mud fenders above them, then blocking out the cab geometry forward of the chassis with a lower body section and a wedge-shaped hood/nose.

Still working out the upper greenhouse and windscreen shape, using slanted boxes for the armored glass with a glowing cyan visor slit, while keeping the nose block positioned forward at z 3.2..4.4.

I'll simplify by making the cab block taller (y 1.1 to 2.7) so there's room for a proper windscreen, then add a glowing cyan visor plate on the front face using an HUD-style glass texture.

Next I'm adding dark glass side windows as slits, door panels with handles and hinges, and roof details like a light bar, antenna, and turret. For the front, I'll give it an armored bumper/bull bar with spikes, a plough plate, and glowing magenta headlight slits.

For the rear, I'm planning hazard chevron textures on the front bumper plate, thin magenta underglow boxes along the chassis, and a sealed cargo pod mounted on a flatbed deck behind the cab, built as a faceted lathe-generated capsule shape.

Painting the pod with a panelled countershade material in pale ceramic tones, then adding orange accent bands as thin ring-shaped lathe shapes matching the pod's octagon segment count, sized slightly larger than the hull radius.

For details, I'm placing a glowing cyan seam ring near the hatch, a red-lit security seal lock on top, and a decal projection for the corp emblem onto the octagonal hull face using a surface-projecting decal method rather than trying to align flat planes manually.

I'm also adding cradle saddle blocks beneath the pod for support, glow-lit clamp brackets, a status screen reading "SEALED" near the rear, and considering a circular rear door detail on the end cap.

Measuring out the pod's length along z and leaving a hitch/conduit gap before the cab, then adding cooling fins and an antenna on top. I'm planning twin turrets—one on the cab roof with yaw/pitch joints and sensor eye, another rear-mounted on the pod—plus angled slat side skirts between the wheels.

Working out skirt placement relative to wheel arches: checking z-ranges for the front axle and rear tandem wheels so the skirt plates clear them, settling on a box roughly 0.08x0.7x2.8 positioned at z 0.55. I'm skipping fuel tanks for now and adding toolboxes instead, then sizing fender boxes to sit above the wheel tops.

Now I'm adjusting the cab geometry so the wheel arches don't clip through the body -- raising the cab bottom to around 1.25-1.3 and adding side fenders, then resizing the cab to span y 1.3..2.8 and the nose to y 1.2..2.1 so everything clears the wheel tops at 1.1. I'm also repositioning the visor near the cab's front face to align with the new nose height.

I'm now checking that the rear wheels don't collide with the deck sides -- with wheel hubs at y 0.55 and deck bottom around 1.05, the wheel x-positions overlap the deck's half-width of 1.25, so I'm narrowing the deck to about 2.0 wide and shifting the wheel centers outward to clear it.

I'm setting up a tandem rear axle arrangement with wheel pairs at z -1.6 and -3.0, giving six wheels total like a dually configuration. I'm writing a reusable wheel-building helper that creates the hub joint, tire cylinder, rim, a glowing neon hub ring, and bolts for each wheel position.

Adding wheel tread lugs...

Now I'm designing the hazard stripe texture as an SVG with diagonal yellow/black stripes for the bumper planes, and planning the texture set: HAZARD, VISOR, LOGO for the pod emblem, and a plain ASCII "SEALED" label since kanji fonts might not render reliably.

I'm settling on six textures total: HAZARD, VISOR, LOGO, STATUS for the rear screen, PLATE for a door number plaque reading something like "CV-77 // ESCORT", and considering an EYE or headlight slit texture too. I'm also laying out underglow neon strips in magenta and cyan along the chassis and pod sides, red taillight glow at the rear deck, and two tall exhaust stacks with caps mounted behind the cab.

For rigging, the chassis gets a spine role with hinge joints at the wheels. I'm sagging a cable between cab and pod using a catmull-rom sweep with end caps, adding whip antennas via a spike primitive, a small lathe-built satellite dish, and an amber light bar glow. I'm also double-checking wheel geometry so the 12-sided cylinder sits flush with the ground without clipping below y=0, accounting for whether a vertex or flat face lands at the bottom.

Checking the lug and wheel radii against total vehicle height to keep any ground sink within a reasonable 2% tolerance, then moving on to setting up the imports and type aliases for colors and paint objects before writing the helper functions.

Writing builder helpers...

Defining color palette and generating texture SVGs for hazard stripes and other surface details...

I'm sketching the visor texture with a gradient background and cyan hud lines, then designing a hexagonal logo mark with the "AEGIS-9" wordmark on a transparent backdrop for decal use, and starting on a status indicator texture.

Now I'm drafting a plate texture labeled "CV-77" and skipping the neon sign asset, then writing a turret helper function that builds a yaw joint hierarchy parented to the chassis, working out the correct bone direction and up-vector so the hinge rotates properly about the vertical axis.

Still writing turret parts...

Now I'm planning the full chassis structure: a spine joint for the chassis, a long frame beam spanning the body length, cross members, axle tubes connecting the wheels, a driveshaft rod, and a differential housing sphere, followed by cab details like the nose block, hood slope, and cab block.

For the cab I'm detailing the roof, visor plate with glow, visor frame boxes, mirror arms, and door assemblies with hinges, panels, glass slits, handles, and decals, positioning them carefully relative to the cab block width. I'm also considering adding angled armor wedge plates on the nose sides for a chevron-style front accent.

Now I'm working out the bumper geometry with a hazard-striped front plane, forward-facing tooth spikes, and a dark grille face with glowing cyan slit lines and slanted amber-white headlights positioned on the nose front.

Checking the nose and cab z-ranges line up without clipping, then moving to the pod cradle: three trim saddles spaced along the frame to support the pod's cylindrical body, making sure the saddle tops clear the pod's curved underside.

I'm skipping the tie-strap rings and adding small clamp brackets with cyan glow near the sides, then positioning seam light bands along the pod's length by shifting their z-centers relative to the pod's axis.

Checking the band geometry: the outer octagon radius of 1.27 keeps its flats above the pod's own flat radius of 1.11, so the band sits properly outside the body without clipping, and the thin glow ring nested just outside that at radius 1.2-1.3 should read clearly against the hull.

Now I'm working out the rear end details — a lock disc cylinder near z=-4.22 with a matching glow torus, and a status screen plane positioned just inside the tapered end cap so it doesn't poke through the hull surface.

Now I'm positioning the hatch joint on the pod's top with a steel ring, glow dot, and vent fins arranged around it, then placing a decal logo on the pod's side using a directional offset.

I'm reasoning through whether the decal text needs mirroring depending on viewing direction, concluding it shouldn't since decals render correctly from the front regardless of side. I'm also considering adding a second decal strip reading "CARGO // SEALED" on the pod.

Then I'm planning rear truck details -- glowing taillight bars, bumper, mud flaps behind the rear wheels, and a hitch -- along with cylindrical fuel tanks mounted between the axles on each side, positioned to clear the wheels, complete with straps and a glow gauge.

Working out the skirt plate placement so it clears the front wheels, with glowing orange edge strips and hazard markings, then starting on the roof with a lightbar featuring amber glowing pods.

Now I'm positioning the roof turret relative to the cab and lightbar, adding an antenna spike and a satellite dish using a lathe profile pointed toward the sky. I'm also planning a glowing cyan sensor lens on the turret and cables sweeping from the cab rear to the pod front.

Writing sweep code...

Now I'm adding magenta underglow strips along the chassis, positioning them clear of the wheels between the axles.

I'm wrapping each part in a glow effect and adding a door decal plane oriented to face outward on the cab. Then I'm planning mirrors with rods and glass boxes, exhaust pipes with heat glow rings, and a rear armor bumper.

Now I'm placing the rear hazard plane, red taillight glow boxes, and a rear panel housing the lights near the pod end, then adding rubber mud flaps positioned just behind each rear wheel.

Checking that the flaps clear the tandem wheels without overlap, then adding armored fenders over the rear wheels and matching front fender plates near the cab.

Tallying part counts across wheel assemblies, lugs, and cylinders to stay safely under the triangle budget. Now I'm starting to write out the wheel joint and hub construction function...

Writing wheel joint code...

I'm fixing the joint direction so the spin axis properly aligns with the X-axis for the wheel's rotation, then setting up the lug bolt loop around the hub.

Now I'm working out the rotation math so each lug box's radial thickness aligns correctly at its angular position around the wheel.

Next I'm adding rim bolts and a glowing neon torus ring to the hub, then sketching out a cylinder helper and starting the turret construction function.

Writing turret joints...

Still writing hull geometry...

Still writing helper functions and types...
